A moment of curiosity

Point. Get the meaning.
Keep reading.

No typing. No switching between apps. Just a quick glance, then back to your book.

01

Point at an unfamiliar word.

Hold the small green ring over the word. A highlight sweeps across it as it’s read.

02

Get the meaning.

The dictionary definition appears. Read it at a glance, or explore other meanings when you need to.

03

Keep reading.

Swipe the definition away and return to your sentence. The camera is ready for the next unfamiliar word. Touch and hold a word in a definition to look it up, copy it or search Google. Return to the original entry when you are done. You can also search Google directly from a scanned word.

Let the sentence help.

When a verified sentence match is ready, its dictionary meaning appears first. Other meanings stay within reach, ready to expand.

Sentence matching requires a supported iPhone with Apple Intelligence available on iOS 26 or later. Otherwise, the first dictionary meaning appears.

Words change shape. We follow.

Plurals and conjugations can lead to their dictionary headwords, so the word on the page can take you to the entry you need.

running → runmangeaient → manger

Reading in English? Add a word translation in your chosen language alongside the English definition. Download its pack once, then use it offline.

Word equivalents vary by word and language. These are individual words, rather than full-page translations.

A word in your language.

Reading an English book? Choose from 24 separate word translation packs: the 23 downloadable book languages above, plus Greek. Translate words from all 23 supported non-English book languages into English. English definitions are optional where compatible translation models are available.

An interface that feels familiar.

26 interface languages. Tap the gear on the home screen, then Settings → App language. It follows your phone language by default; unsupported phone languages use English. This does not change the book language.

Greek has an interface and English-word translations, but is not a book language. Kurdish covers Latin-script Kurmanji, not Sorani; Malay covers Latin-script Rumi. Chinese supports Simplified and Traditional text. Coverage varies by word, form and language.

Before you turn the page

A few good
questions.

Need a hand? Get in touch ↗
Does Booktionary work offline?

Yes. English definitions are built in. Download any additional dictionaries or translation packs while you’re online; once installed, they work without a connection. Checking the language catalog also needs internet access.

Which languages can I read?

The 24 book languages are listed above. English is built in; the other 23 dictionaries download separately. Choose the language of your book before reading. Chinese supports Simplified and Traditional text; Kurdish covers Latin-script Kurmanji and Malay covers Rumi.

Can I translate the word or the whole definition?

Word translations appear beside English definitions. On iOS 18 or later, you can also opt into translated definitions for English books in 19 supported languages after downloading the required files. Translate words from all 23 supported non-English book languages into English. English definitions are optional where compatible translation models are available.

How does the app choose a meaning?

When a verified sentence match is ready, its dictionary meaning appears first. Other meanings stay within reach, ready to expand. Sentence matching requires a supported iPhone with Apple Intelligence available on iOS 26 or later. Otherwise, the first dictionary meaning appears.

Will it work with my iPhone?

Booktionary requires an iPhone running iOS 17 or later. Good light and a clear printed page help the camera recognise words.

Do you collect my reading data?

Google search is optional, opens your browser and requires internet. Only when you choose it is the search text sent to Google. Camera images remain on your iPhone. There are no accounts, ads or analytics. Dictionary downloads contact the content host, which can receive connection details such as your IP address.

Tips

  • Good light helps more than anything else.
  • If nothing is recognised, move the phone nearer the page. About 15 cm works well.
  • A slight tilt is fine. The app reads text at a natural reading angle.
  • The ring never moves and never changes colour. It marks where the app is looking; the highlight sweeping across the word is what tells you it has been read.
  • Swipe the definition away to return to the camera.
